Formerly a very recognisable Canadian consumer brand; now defunct as a retailer.

Extremely visible consumer fashion brand, driven by celebrity and social media, and official underwear partner of Team USA.

Hugo Boss is a Metzingen, Germany fashion house, founded in 1924, selling menswear and womenswear under the BOSS and HUGO labels, plus fragrances licensed to Interparfums. Sold through own stores, e-commerce, wholesale and outlets in over 100 countries, with revenue near 4.2 billion euros. Listed on the Frankfurt exchange (BOSS). Premium consumer brand with strong visibility, a long-time sponsor of Formula 1 and sports such as Formula E, with an F1 history of driver apparel.

Miniso is a Guangzhou, China-based lifestyle products retailer founded in 2013 by Ye Guofu, selling affordable home goods, accessories, toys and cosmetics with design-led branding and Japanese-style positioning. It has over 7,000 stores in about 100 countries, mostly franchised, including licensed IP collections such as Sanrio and Disney. Listed on the NYSE (MNSO) and in Hong Kong (9896). High consumer awareness in Asia and growing in Western markets.

Rent the Runway is a New York online fashion rental platform founded in 2009 by Jennifer Hyman and Jennifer Fleiss, letting customers rent designer dresses and clothing by subscription or per item, with some resale. It is based in New York with distribution hubs in the US and a few retail locations. It listed on Nasdaq (RENT) in 2021; revenue is about $300 million. Strong brand among US women, well-known for fashion marketing.

Under Armour is a Baltimore-based sportswear company founded in 1996 by Kevin Plank, making performance apparel, footwear and accessories sold through wholesale, own stores and e-commerce in North America, EMEA and Asia-Pacific. Annual revenue is about $5 billion. Listed on NYSE (UAA, UA). Customers are athletes and sports consumers. Very high consumer brand awareness, with major sponsorship deals in athletics, college sports and golf.

Gap Inc. is a US apparel retailer headquartered in San Francisco and listed on the NYSE (GAP). It owns Gap, Old Navy, Banana Republic and Athleta, selling clothing and accessories through roughly 3,500 company-operated and franchise stores and online in the US and abroad, with annual revenue around 15 billion dollars. Customers are mainstream consumers; money comes from retail sales. Founded 1969. One of the most recognised fashion brands globally, with large consumer reach and marketing partnerships.

VF Corporation is a US apparel and footwear company headquartered in Denver, Colorado and listed on the NYSE (VFC). Its brands include The North Face, Vans, Timberland, Dickies, Kipling and Eastpak; the Supreme streetwear brand was sold in 2024. It sells through wholesale, its own stores and e-commerce in about 100 countries, with revenue near 10 billion dollars. Founded 1899 as Vanity Fair Mills. Customers are consumers in outdoor, active and workwear segments. Highly visible consumer brands with strong action-sports and outdoor marketing.

Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail (ABFRL) is a large Indian branded apparel and fashion retailer, headquartered in Mumbai and listed on the NSE and BSE, part of the Aditya Birla Group. Brands include Louis Philippe, Van Heusen, Allen Solly, Peter England, Pantaloons and a stake in designer labels, sold through thousands of stores and online. Revenue is around 140 billion rupees, with the premium Madura brand business demerged in 2025. Strong mass and premium consumer brands in India, with celebrity and cricket marketing.

ASOS is a British online fashion retailer headquartered in London and listed on the London Stock Exchange (ASC). It sells over 85,000 products, including its own labels and hundreds of third-party brands, to young shoppers in more than 190 countries from distribution centres in the UK, US and Germany, with revenue near 2.9 billion pounds and around 20 million active customers. Founded 2000 as As Seen On Screen. Very strong youth fashion brand with heavy social media marketing.

Dillard's is a US department store chain headquartered in Little Rock, Arkansas and listed on the NYSE (DDS). It operates about 270 full-line stores and clearance centres in 29 states plus online, selling apparel, cosmetics, home goods and accessories with a mid-to-upper price positioning and private labels such as Antonio Melani. Revenue is around 6.5 billion dollars. Founded 1938 and run by the Dillard family. Well-known regional US retail brand with a loyal older customer base.

Warby Parker is a US eyewear company headquartered in New York and listed on the NYSE (WRBY), selling prescription glasses, sunglasses and contact lenses through about 300 retail stores and online, with home try-on and an eye exam offering. Customers are mainstream consumers, with revenue near 800 million dollars. Founded 2010 with a buy-a-pair give-a-pair model. Strong direct-to-consumer lifestyle brand among younger consumers.

Levi Strauss & Co. is the US denim and apparel company headquartered in San Francisco and listed on the NYSE (LEVI). Its Levi's jeans, Dockers (sold in 2025 to Authentic Brands), Signature by Levi Strauss and Beyond Yoga brands are sold through wholesale, 3,000-plus own and franchised stores and online in over 100 countries, with revenue near 6 billion dollars. Founded 1853. Customers are mainstream consumers worldwide. One of the best-known apparel brands in the world with long sports and music marketing.

Coupang is a South Korean e-commerce giant based in Seattle that runs the Coupang marketplace, Rocket Delivery fast shipping, Rocket Wow membership, Coupang Eats food delivery, Coupang Play streaming and Taiwan expansion, with revenue of around $30 billion and tens of millions of customers. Founded in 2010 by Bom Kim. Listed on NYSE (CPNG) since 2021, with SoftBank Vision Fund a major early investor. Dominant Korean consumer brand with heavy advertising.

Online luxury fashion retailer formed by the 2015 merger of Yoox and Net-a-Porter, operating Net-a-Porter, Mr Porter, The Outnet and Yoox, selling designer clothing to affluent consumers in 180 countries. Owned by Richemont until Mytheresa's parent LuxExperience acquired the group in 2025. High brand visibility among luxury shoppers. The group employs thousands of people and operates warehouses and fulfilment centres in Europe, the US and Asia.

US department store retailer headquartered in Seattle, founded 1901, selling fashion, beauty and homeware through about 360 Nordstrom and Nordstrom Rack stores and online. Revenue is about $15 billion. Taken private in 2025 by the Nordstrom family and Mexico's Liverpool. Strong consumer brand in the US and Canada. Nordstrom has about 60,000 employees, including its off-price Nordstrom Rack stores and the Trunk Club brand.

Luxury fashion house founded 1910 by Gabrielle Chanel in Paris, selling haute couture, ready-to-wear, leather goods, fragrance (No. 5), makeup, watches and jewellery. Privately owned by the Wertheimer family, with revenue around $20 billion. The input lists a London HQ for Chanel Ltd, but the group is Paris-run. Among the world's most recognised luxury brands. Chanel has about 30,000 employees and a global network of boutiques, and does not sell through third-party websites.

Telgte-based German value fashion retailer, with about 1,900 stores across Europe, owned by Apax and other lenders. Consumer brand in Germany and Europe. Known for low prices; around 1,800 stores. Consumer brand in Germany, Austria, and elsewhere in Europe. Takko was founded in 1982 and is owned by lenders after restructuring and prior ownership by Advent. It sells clothing for women, men and children at low prices through shops in Germany, Austria, Poland, Czechia and other markets.

BVI Medical is a manufacturer and marketer of specialised ophthalmic surgical devices, including cataract and retinal surgery instruments, intraocular lenses and glaucoma implants, sold to surgeons and hospitals worldwide. Headquartered in Waltham, Massachusetts, it grew out of Beaver-Visitec International and is privately held and owned by private equity investors. B2B medical products with no consumer visibility; very limited sponsorship fit.

about: Allbirds is a San Francisco footwear and apparel brand known for its Wool Runner and Tree Runner sneakers made from merino wool and eucalyptus fibre, with a sustainability and carbon-footprint-labelling angle. It sells through its own stores and website, plus wholesale, in the US, Europe and Asia, and listed on Nasdaq (BIRD) in 2021 at a valuation above 2 billion dollars. Founded in 2016, it has since seen collapsing sales and a much lower valuation. Widely recognised lifestyle consumer brand, particularly in the US.

OVS S.p.A. is an Italian fashion retailer, with around 1,000 stores of the OVS, OVS Kids and Upim brands, selling affordable clothing for men, women and children, and the Stefanel brand after a later acquisition. Customers are mass-market Italian consumers, with growing international franchising. Founded in 1972 as part of Coin group and headquartered in Venice-Mestre, it listed on the Milan stock exchange (OVS) in 2015. Revenue is over 1.5 billion euros. Very well known household retail brand in Italy.

New Era Cap is a Buffalo, New York headwear and apparel company, founded in 1920, known for the 59FIFTY fitted baseball cap and as the official on-field cap supplier to Major League Baseball. It sells through retailers and e-commerce in over 100 countries, with licences for leagues such as the NFL and NBA. Recorded funding of about $775 million reflects a minority investment. Very strong consumer brand, already active in sports merchandise.

CaratLane is an Indian omnichannel jewellery brand, founded in 2008 and headquartered in Chennai, now majority-owned by Titan Company (Tata Group) since 2023. It sells diamond, gold and gemstone jewellery online and through about 300 stores. Funding shown is about $614 million. Strong and growing consumer brand in India, with a young audience.

Lands' End is a Dodgeville, Wisconsin apparel and home goods retailer, listed on Nasdaq (LE), selling casual clothing, outerwear, swimwear and school uniforms through its website, catalogues and stores. Revenue is about $1.4 billion, and the company was formerly owned by Sears Holdings. Customers are mid-market US families. Well-known consumer brand with an older audience.

Luxury fashion e-commerce platform founded in 2011 and based in New York, connecting shoppers with designer brands via a trunk-show and pre-order model, selling women's designer clothing, shoes, bags and jewellery online. Customers are high-income consumers worldwide; revenue comes from product sales and commission on designer goods. Has raised around USD 417 million from investors. Recognised in luxury fashion circles, modest mass-market visibility.

Milan-based Italian luxury group founded in 1910, making menswear and tailoring under the Zegna brand, Thom Browne and Tom Ford Fashion. Sells through its own stores, wholesale and e-commerce worldwide, with revenue of around EUR 1.9 billion. Listed on the NYSE (ZGN) since 2021 after a SPAC merger; the Zegna family controls it. Strong luxury consumer brand, sells in about 80 markets.

Toronto-based luxury outdoor apparel maker famous for down-filled parkas. Designs and sells cold-weather jackets and apparel through its own stores, e-commerce and wholesale in more than 50 countries, with revenue about CAD 1.3 billion. Listed on NYSE and TSX (GOOS), controlled by Bain Capital. Premium consumer brand with high awareness and fashion and celebrity presence.

German optician chain founded 1972 in Hamburg and Europe's largest by volume, selling glasses, contact lenses and hearing aids through about 1,000 stores in Germany, Austria, Switzerland and elsewhere, with revenue above EUR 2 billion. Listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange (FIE) and family-controlled. Mass-market consumer brand in Germany, known for heavy advertising.

US apparel group in New York owning Calvin Klein and Tommy Hilfiger, selling clothing, underwear, footwear and accessories globally in thousands of stores and online, with revenue about USD 9 billion. Listed on the NYSE (PVH). Brands are household names; Calvin Klein and Tommy Hilfiger have strong global awareness and previous sports sponsorship.

US children's apparel retailer based in Secaucus, New Jersey, selling kids' clothing through roughly 500 stores and online in North America. Listed on Nasdaq (PLCE) and under financial pressure in recent years. Brands are The Children's Place, Gymboree, Sugar & Jade and PLACE Sports, founded in 1969, with franchise partners operating in about 20 other countries. Mass-market family consumer brand with solid US awareness.

Shenzhen company providing internet-enabled solutions for the textile industry, with software and enterprise tags in the input. Customers are presumably textile makers using SaaS tools. No scale or ownership is stated. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: German department store chain Galeria, formerly Galeria Karstadt Kaufhof, with about 80 stores selling fashion, beauty and household goods. It went through insolvency twice, in 2020 and 2022 and 2023. Customers are German shoppers. Galeria sought insolvency protection in 2020, 2022 and January 2024, and was taken over in 2024 by Richard Baker and Bernd Beetz after the collapse of owner Signa. Consumer retail brand with strong awareness in Germany.
Canadian/US-based retail group, owner of Garage and Dynamite apparel brands, 2025 IPO on Toronto. Sells fashion in malls across North America and Europe. Consumer brand.

Indian online jewellery brand GIVA, selling silver jewellery to consumers, based in Bengaluru and backed by Fireside Ventures. Customers are young Indian women shopping online. Consumer brand with strong social media presence and growing awareness.

Vestis is a Roswell, Georgia uniform and workplace supplies rental company, spun off from Aramark in 2023, serving about 300,000 business customers in the US and Canada with uniforms, floor mats, restroom supplies and first aid products through a network of plants. Listed on the NYSE (VSTS). Revenue is about $2.8 billion. B2B service with low consumer awareness.

Farfetch is a London-based online luxury fashion marketplace, founded in 2007 by Jose Neves, connecting boutiques and brands with consumers in about 190 countries and owning Browns, Stadium Goods and New Guards (Off-White). Coupang acquired it in a rescue deal in 2024 after it struggled and was delisted from the NYSE. Strong luxury consumer brand with sports and fashion collaborations.

Secoo is a Beijing based Chinese online and offline luxury retailer selling fashion, watches, jewellery and lifestyle goods through an app, website and physical stores. It listed on Nasdaq (SECO) in 2019, and later had financial difficulties, with delisting and debt issues in 2022-2023. Funding shown is about $666 million. It served affluent Chinese consumers. It was a reasonably known luxury e-commerce brand in China, but its recent status is uncertain.

about: Tanger is a Greensboro, North Carolina real estate investment trust that owns and operates open-air outlet shopping centers, with about 30 properties in the US and Canada, leased to retail brands. Revenue comes from rent from tenants and sponsorship, and it attracts shoppers to destinations like Tanger Outlets. It was founded in 1981 and is listed on the NYSE (SKT). It is a recognized consumer retail destination brand in the US.

Brands For Less is a Dubai based online and offline fashion discount retailer, selling clothing, shoes, bags and home items from international brands at reduced prices across the Middle East. Crunchbase shows funding of about $360 million. It has stores in the UAE and a website, and a recognisable consumer brand in the Gulf region.

about: Synsam Group is a Stockholm based Nordic optical retailer operating about 600 eyewear and optician stores in Sweden, Norway, Finland and Denmark under the Synsam and other brands, also producing its own lenses and eyewear. It listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (SYNSAM) in 2021. Its customers are consumers buying glasses, contact lenses and eye tests. It is a major Nordic consumer retail brand with a heavy advertising presence.

Tradeinn is a Girona, Catalonia, Spain based e-commerce group running a network of about 11 specialist online stores for sports and outdoor gear, including Tradeinn, Diveinn, Bikeinn, Runnerinn, Trekkinn and Kidinn. It ships from a large central warehouse to customers in many countries and offers thousands of brands. Founded in 2006, it is privately held, with Crunchbase funding of about 200 million euros. It is a consumer online retailer, well known among sports and outdoor enthusiasts in Europe.

SRTX (SRTX Labs) is a Montreal based Canadian materials company creating advanced textiles and fibres for fashion, sportswear and industrial uses, according to Crunchbase, with funding recorded of about $191 million. The input gives no details of its products, customers or ownership, and the name is unfamiliar. It is probably a B2B materials developer with limited brand awareness. about: Dolce & Gabbana is an Italian luxury fashion house founded in 1985 in Milan by Domenico Dolce and Stefano Gabbana. It sells ready-to-wear, accessories, eyewear, fragrance, beauty and jewellery through a global store network and e-commerce, with revenue above 1.3 billion euros. It is privately held by its founders. The brand has attracted controversy, including in China in 2018, but remains one of the most recognised luxury names. The record shows funding of about 150 million euros, likely debt.

LPP is a Polish fashion retail group based in Gdansk, owning the brands Reserved, Cropp, House, Mohito and Sinsay, sold through thousands of stores and online in Poland, Central and Eastern Europe, the Baltics, and expanding into Western Europe and the Middle East. Founded in 1991, it is listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange (LPP) with revenue above 4 billion euros. Strong consumer brands in Poland and the region.

Purple Style Labs is an Indian fashion and lifestyle retail company based in Mumbai, behind Pernia's Pop-Up Shop, a luxury and designer fashion platform selling Indian designer wear for women, men and brides online and through stores in India, the US and the UAE. Founded in 2012, it has venture backing. Consumer brand with a following among affluent Indian and diaspora shoppers.

Reformation is a US sustainable women's fashion brand, with its corporate base in Los Angeles (the input lists Vernon Hills, Illinois). It sells dresses, tops, denim and shoes through its own stores and online. Founded in 2009, it was acquired by Permira in 2023 and has dozens of stores. Strong consumer brand known for sustainability messaging and celebrity customers.

Burlington Stores is a US off-price retailer of apparel, shoes, home goods and accessories, formerly Burlington Coat Factory, headquartered in Burlington, New Jersey. It operates over 1,000 stores in the US and Puerto Rico, selling branded goods at discounted prices, with annual sales near 10 billion dollars. Listed on the NYSE (BURL). Strong consumer brand across the US, particularly among value-seeking shoppers.
